standard_prerequisites.name: Local cohomology H^i_{V(I)}(M) of a module with support in the closed subset V(I), and its localisation formula H^i_{V(I)}(M)_\mathfrak p = H^i_{\mathfrak pA_\mathfrak p}(M_\mathfrak p)
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's section on generalities about local cohomology, in which the counted statement occurs
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the two modules compared by the counted map and the local vanishing hypothesis.

standard_prerequisites.name: The lemma that elements of a local cohomology module come from a strictly bigger finitely generated ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Author lemma lemma-elements-come-from-bigger, whose statement is reproduced verbatim as a context span of this card (source lines 451-470)
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the step that increases the auxiliary ideal in both halves of the proof and thereby contradicts maximality.

core_obligations: Surjectivity: given a class in H^i_{V(I)}(M), the proof chooses among the finitely generated ideals I \subset I'' \subset I' one maximal with the property that the class lifts from H^i_{V(I'')}(M) (proof lines 509-513)

The maximality contradiction: if V(I'') is properly contained in V(I'), the proof picks a generic point of V(I'') outside V(I') where the local cohomology vanishes by hypothesis, and uses the auxiliary lemma to increase I'', contradicting maximality (proof lines 513-517)

Injectivity: the same maximality argument is run for a class in the kernel of the map, with the vanishing hypothesis shifted by one degree, and the auxiliary lemma again produces the contradiction (proof lines 520-528)
The isomorphism: the third assertion is the conjunction of the first two and is recorded as formal (proof line 531)
proof_roadmap: 满射：取 ξ ∈ H^i_{V(I)}(M)，在 {I'' : I ⊂ I'' ⊂ I'} 中取使 ξ 可提升的最大者。若不是 I'，取 V(I'') 的 generic point p ∉ V(I')，由假设 H^i_{pA_p}(M_p) = 0，再用「元素来自更大理想」的引理把 I'' 放大，矛盾。
单射：对 Ψ 的核中元素 ξ' 做同样的最大性论证，假设换成 H^{i-1} 的消失。(3) 由 (1)(2) 形式给出。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement gives a three-part criterion, in terms of the vanishing of the local cohomology of the module at the primes of V(I) that do not lie in V(I'), for the comparison map between the local cohomology with support in V(I') and with support in V(I) to be surjective, injective, or bijective (author lemma at source lines 485-506, label lemma-isomorphism). The proof (source lines 508-532) runs a maximality argument on the finitely generated ideals between I and I' for an arbitrary class and its kernel class, and in each case produces the contradiction by choosing a generic point of the strictly larger closed set, invoking the vanishing hypothesis there and the chapter's lifting lemma (statement reproduced as a context span) to enlarge the ideal further (proof lines 513-528). The maximality argument in both degrees is the content. H2.
